summary: Intermittent 502/503s and serving-runtime exits observed during tenant high-concurrency burst; socket half-open and ALPN negotiation mismatch suspected
description:
Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10 14:05 and ongoing, customers (LexiSearch dedicated tenant) experienced an elevated error rate (502/503) and several serving-runtime worker exits correlated with a high-concurrency embedding+chat workload. Impact: impacting 12% of requests for tenant; streams reset and a subset of requests returned 502/503. Environment: prod us-east-1 dedicated pool serving redwood/llama3-13b.

Observed behavior: API gateway returned intermittent 502/503s; serving-runtime processes logged SIGTERM/segfault-like exits followed by rapid respawns; edge proxy logs show repeated FIN_WAIT/half-open sockets and ALPN negotiation failures to a small fraction (~0.6%) of upstream handshakes. Expected behavior: sustained tenant traffic should remain under SLA with graceful backpressure and no runtime exits or elevated 5xx floor.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use LexiSearch test harness to replay tenant traffic pattern (mixed streaming chat + batch embedding at 600 TPS peak).
2) Target the dedicated routing tag for LexiSearch in us-east-1.
3) Observe API gateway latencies, edge-proxy socket state counts, and serving-runtime worker process health during ramp to steady-state.
logs: edge-proxy: observed repeated TCP half-open sockets; last packet timestamps show delayed FIN by 15-30s (logs/edge/us-east/2026-03-10.log: lines 5420-5438)
api-gateway: 502 responses spike from baseline 0.2% to 12% between 14:05-14:28 (dashboards/request-errors/us-east)
serving-runtime: worker_42 exited with SIGABRT; stack shows libuv accept loop + pending ALPN callback (logs/runtime/pool-lexi/2026-03-10.err)
kernel: ephemeral port reuse warnings and socket TIME_WAIT backlog briefly exceeded threshold on some hosts (host-monitoring/host-17)
sre traces: trace IDs 01F8... and 01F9... show client kept-alive but did not complete TLS close; upstream reported handshake_retry in one in 2000 connections.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: surge in concurrent streams pushed edge-proxy accept queue into a pathological state, leaving half-open sockets that later cause upstream runtime to hit fd/socket limits and crash.

Observed ALPN negotiation failures are rare but correlate temporally with the first runtime exits; hypothesis: older runtime kernel path triggered a fallback with higher memory pressure during renegotiation.
Checked autoscaler metrics: Dedicated pool scaled as expected but memory fragmentation increased after repeated worker respawns (nvml metrics + runtime memmap).

Heap/stack traces from crashes point to accept/uv_loop handling; adding extra logging to runtime accept path (temporary debug build) reproduced a similar crash in staging when we artificially limited file descriptors.
timeline: 2026-03-10 14:02 - LexiSearch reports elevated 502s via support channel.
2026-03-10 14:06 - Support triaged and created SUP-209824; SRE paged.
2026-03-10 14:15 - SRE confirmed correlated runtime exits on dedicated hosts (pool-lexi-*) and increased socket TIME_WAIT counts.
2026-03-10 14:25 - Temporary route weight shift away from a small subset of edge hosts reduced error rate from 12% -> 3%.
2026-03-10 15:05 - Applied temporary runtime flag to enable aggressive connection reaper; observed further reduction to ~0.5% error rate.
2026-03-11 09:10 - Created infra PR to add ALPN-negotiation fallback and fd limit guard (PR #5678).
2026-03-12 10:00 - Running extended soak in staging with fix; no reproductions so far.
comments: Support (Aisha Patel) - 2026-03-10 14:09: 'Customer reporting streaming disconnects and elevated 502s. Customer impact: production search queries failing intermittently; provided logs and tenant id to SRE.'

SRE (Daniel Kim) - 2026-03-10 14:20: 'Investigating runtime worker exits; collecting core dumps and enabling extra logging on pool-lexi hosts. Early signs point to accept loop hitting stale socket state.'
Customer (LexiSearch Ops) - 2026-03-10 14:35: 'We saw increased latency and a handful of failed user requests; paused some bulk embedding jobs — thanks for the quick mitigation.'
SRE (Priya Nair) - 2026-03-10 15:08: 'Shifted route weights and toggled connection reaper; error floor dropped significantly. Continuing root cause analysis.'
Eng (Riley Chen) - 2026-03-11 09:25: 'Opened PR to add ALPN fallback and to harden accept loop around fd exhaustion; tests in staging are green.'
mitigation: Short term: shift route weight off of affected edge hosts and enable aggressive connection reaper. Customer bulk jobs paused at their side. Longer term: deploy PR to add ALPN fallback and fd-guard in serving runtime; add autoscaler hysteresis to avoid thrashing replicas.
root_cause: Combination of edge-proxy accept-queue pressure during tenant concurrency ramp and an outdated runtime accept path that did not gracefully handle ALPN handshake retries and file descriptor pressure. Resulted in half-open sockets and subsequent runtime process exits that amplified the 5xx rate.
resolution: In progress. Temporary mitigations reduced errors to acceptable levels. Code fix merged (PR #5678) and under staging validation. Plan: staged rollout to canary subset of dedicated pool, monitor errors and socket metrics, then full rollout after 48h clean soak.
follow_up_actions: 1) Roll out PR #5678 to 10% canary in dedicated pools and monitor for 72h.
2) Add alert for edge-proxy half-open socket ratio and tie to automated route-weight throttling.
3) Increase runtime logging around ALPN and accept loop for 7 days post-rollout.
4) Post-incident: write runbook entry for fast shift-and-reap mitigation and document fd/ALPN guard limits.
